result.summary: The new setting is persisted but cannot be edited through the UI and does not control shutdown behavior.

findings.title: Connect the saved timeout to shutdown draining
findings.body: Posting shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 now succeeds and persists that value, but scheduler.py:81 still initializes the drain timeout exclusively from the environment, and scheduler.py:634 uses that constant. With no environment override, shutdown still times out after 60 seconds, regardless of the saved setting or a restart. Operators cannot obtain the longer drain period this endpoint now accepts.
findings.recommendation: Read the current general.shutdown_drain_timeout at shutdown, retaining the intended environment override, and test that saving 120.5 changes the effective drain timeout.

findings.title: Add the form input for the newly persisted setting
findings.body: The added template context has no corresponding input in settings.html. Users cannot view or edit the timeout, and browser submissions omit it, causing the new save logic to write 60.0. Thus a value of 120.5 saved through a direct POST is reset by the next ordinary settings save. The existing rendering assertion in tests/test_web.py:694 also requires this missing field.
findings.recommendation: Add a numeric shutdown_drain_timeout input associated with settings-form, render the current value, and support fractional values with the same bounds as the handler. Preserve the current value when the field is omitted.

next_steps: Complete the template and scheduler integration, then verify rendering, browser-form round trips, and effective shutdown timing.
